topic: Why mutating a ref's .current property during the render phase violates React's concurrent rendering model and causes unpredictable, hard-to-debug UI tearing

Why using the `delete` keyword to remove a property from an object transitions V8 to dictionary mode, permanently destroying the hidden class (Shape) optimization and causing massive performance drops in hot paths

Why wrapping a state update in `startTransition` still blocks the UI during expensive renders unless the slow components are memoized, because React still has to execute the entire tree's render phase.
Why an unused large variable leaks memory in JavaScript when an adjacent closure in the same lexical scope is retained, due to how V8 shares closure contexts across functions
Why pre-allocating arrays with 'new Array(size)' or manually resizing them via 'length' transitions V8 to 'holey' element kinds, permanently degrading iteration performance compared to packed arrays

Why using React 19's new `use` hook to resolve a Promise inside a component causes an infinite re-render loop if the Promise is instantiated directly during render instead of being cached with `React.cache` or `useMemo`

Why throwing an error inside a `new Promise` executor function fails to reject the promise if the throw occurs inside an asynchronous callback (like `setTimeout`), leading to uncaught runtime exceptions instead of a rejected promise.

Why omitting the 'await' keyword when returning a Promise inside a try-catch block causes rejected promises to bypass the local catch block entirely, and why the deprecated 'no-return-await' ESLint rule contributed to this widespread misunderstanding.

Why passing an inline arrow function as a React ref callback causes it to execute twice on every update—first with null and then with the DOM element—and how to stabilize the reference to prevent redundant initialization logic.

Why reading mutable global variables or browser APIs directly inside a React component's render phase causes visual 'tearing' under concurrent rendering, and how `useSyncExternalStore` prevents this by forcing a synchronous fallback when mutations occur mid-render.

Why calling a React 19 Server Action imperatively inside an event handler fails to trigger pending states in 'useTransition' or 'useActionState' unless manually wrapped in 'startTransition', unlike passing it directly to a form's action attribute

Why wrapping a class instance that uses private fields (#field) in a JavaScript Proxy throws a runtime TypeError when calling methods that access those fields, due to private brand checks failing on the proxy receiver instead of the underlying target
